title: Simple Garlic Pasta
summary: Spaghetti with slow-toasted garlic, olive oil and a splash of starchy pasta water that turns into a glossy sauce. Five ingredients, one pot and one pan, and a timer so the pasta comes out al dente every time.

ingredients.name: spaghetti
ingredients.notes: or linguine; check the package for its own al dente time

ingredients.name: garlic
ingredients.notes: slices, not minced, so they toast instead of burn

steps.instruction: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil and add the salt. Slice the garlic while you wait.
success_cues: Water is at a full, rolling boil, not just steaming
Water tastes noticeably salty, like a mild broth
steps.creator_note: Salt the water more than feels right. It is the only chance to season the pasta itself.

steps.instruction: Add the spaghetti and stir for the first 30 seconds so it does not stick. Set a timer for 2 minutes less than the package time; you will finish the pasta in the pan.
success_cues: Strands have gone limp and are fully under the water

steps.instruction: Meanwhile, put the olive oil and sliced garlic in a cold, wide skillet and set it over medium-low heat. Let the garlic warm up slowly with the oil, swirling now and then, for 4 to 6 minutes.
success_cues: Garlic slices turn pale gold and smell sweet, not sharp
Tiny steady bubbles around each slice, never a loud sizzle
warnings: If the garlic turns brown it is bitter; start again with fresh garlic rather than pushing on. Keep the heat low.
steps.creator_note: Starting the garlic in cold oil is the whole recipe. Hot oil browns the outside before the inside sweetens.

steps.instruction: When the garlic is golden, add the red pepper flakes if using, then ladle about half a cup of the starchy pasta water into the skillet. It will spit for a second and then calm down. Keep the pan on low.
success_cues: Oil and water come together into a cloudy, slightly thickened liquid
warnings: Hot oil spits when water hits it; add the water away from your body and stand back.

steps.instruction: When the timer goes, bite a strand: it should be al dente, tender with a thin, firm white core in the centre. Scoop another cup of pasta water out of the pot, then drain the pasta.
success_cues: Bitten through, there is a pinpoint of firm, chalky white at the centre
steps.creator_note: Al dente means it still has bite. If there is no white core, you are already past it; drain immediately.

steps.instruction: Tip the drained pasta into the skillet. Raise the heat to medium and toss constantly for 1 to 2 minutes, adding splashes of the reserved water, until the oil and water tighten into a sauce that coats every strand.
success_cues: Sauce looks glossy and clings to the pasta instead of pooling in the pan
No watery puddle left when you tilt the skillet

steps.instruction: Off the heat, toss in the parsley, parmesan and lemon zest if using. Taste for salt and serve right away.
success_cues: Cheese melts into the sauce without clumping
Strands still slide apart rather than sticking in a block

creator_notes: Package times are usually a minute or two too long for al dente. Pull it early; it keeps cooking in the pan.
No parmesan? A spoon of butter at the end gives the same richness.
dietary_warnings: Contains wheat (gluten). Parmesan is optional and contains milk.
